title: Dates and times
summary: to_datetime with formats and coerced errors, the .dt accessor, date arithmetic, date-range filters, and monthly resampling.
hints: `parse_timestamps`: `df.assign(timestamp=pd.to_datetime(df["timestamp"], format="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", errors="coerce"))`: anything that does not match becomes `NaT`. `add_date_parts` (on parsed data): `ts = df["timestamp"].dt`, then `year=ts.year`, `month=ts.month`, `weekday=ts.day_name()`.

`count_between`: compare dates, not times: `day = df["timestamp"].dt.normalize()` (midnight of each day), then `day.between(pd.Timestamp(start), pd.Timestamp(end)).sum()`; wrap in `int(...)`. `late_orders`: `(pd.to_datetime(df["shipped"]) - pd.to_datetime(df["ordered"])).dt.days` gives whole days.

`monthly_totals`: drop rows with a missing timestamp, then `df.set_index("timestamp")["amount"].resample("MS").sum()`. `"MS"` means "month start" bins, and months with no rows appear with 0. Build the dict with `{ts.strftime("%Y-%m"): float(v) for ts, v in totals.items()}`.
